context.alert_text: Unhealthy hosts in the MQTT target group above 0

root_cause.hypothesis: The UnhealthyHostCount=1 alarm reflects transient target churn from routine EC2 Auto Scaling activity (repeated Deregister/Register cycles on the target group) rather than an application or load-balancer failure. The ASG is replacing an instance (scale-in/out or health-check replacement), and one target briefly reports unhealthy during the swap while the other targets remain healthy.
evidence: Repeated DeregisterTargets/RegisterTargets pairs by the AutoScaling service role in the 20 minutes before the alarm
No change on the load balancer itself
4 other targets remain healthy per the sibling metric
ruled_out: Load balancer misconfiguration (C2 shows no change on the LB)
Widespread outage (M2 shows 4 healthy hosts still in service)

proposal.reasoning: The alarm fired on a single unhealthy host (1/1 datapoint, Maximum stat) while 4 sibling targets remain healthy, and the preceding changes are routine AutoScaling-driven Register/Deregister cycles with no change to the load balancer or target group configuration itself. This pattern is consistent with normal instance replacement churn in a dev environment rather than a systemic failure requiring intervention. No deploy, config, or LB-state evidence points to a fault needing remediation.
proposal.expected_effect: No change; the target group is expected to self-heal as the ASG-driven instance replacement completes and the new instance passes health checks (HealthyThresholdCount=3).
